paper.title: SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents
paper.central_claim: An RL recipe (grouped task streams + composite reward) trains a skill curator that edits an external Markdown SkillRepo for a frozen executor; the learned curator outperforms memory-free and memory-based baselines (and a Gemini-2.5-Pro prompted curator) in effectiveness and efficiency, and generalizes across executors and task domains.

signatures.information: Curator sees trajectory, self-judged correctness, and BM25-retrieved related skills; executor frozen, retrieves top-5 skills by BM25; no gold label at curation time; training reward uses downstream task outcomes over a grouped stream
signatures.operation: After each task the curator emits a sequence of insert_skill/update_skill/delete_skill function calls that ApplyOps to the repo
signatures.output: S_{t+1}=ApplyOps(S_t, c_t); repo read by executor on subsequent tasks
signatures.conditions: streaming task sequence; tool-call schema (Fig 8); skill = YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

signatures.selection_rule_data: No per-edit acceptance gate: all curator ops are applied; selection happens only through GRPO updating the curator (8 rollouts of the whole curation sequence per group, advantage = reward minus group mean) on the training split
signatures.persistence: SkillRepo persists within the stream; curator weights persist after RL; repo reset to empty at start of each training group
signatures.later_use: BM25 top-5 retrieval into executor prompt on later tasks
signatures.claimed_effect: ALFWorld avg SR 55.7 -> 61.2 vs ReasoningBank (Qwen3-8B exec), fewer steps; WebShop SR 16.5 vs 11.4; reasoning avg 73.8 vs 69.6
signatures.failure_boundary: Flat single-file skills; BM25 retrieval; frozen executor; no rollback/version/staleness mechanism; agentic gains larger than reasoning gains

gap.author_gap: Skill curation is the bottleneck; manual, heuristic-prescribed and short-horizon RL curation cannot learn complex long-term curation (update/delete) from indirect, delayed feedback.
gap.checked_gap: Real and specific: prior fixed curators (ReasoningBank, MemP) use hand rules; RL-trained curators exist (Mem-alpha, Ye et al. 2026, ARISE) but the paper only asserts, not tests, that their short horizon is the limiting factor. The SkillOS-base vs SkillOS vs SkillOS-gemini rows do show curation quality matters in this setting.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus. The load-bearing move is manufacturing a training signal for curation decisions that have no per-decision label. Grouped task streams let later related tasks score earlier edits, and the outcome signal is self-judged by the frozen executor (opus:O02) plus an LLM content judge. That matches self_supervised_signal_engineering, with no C-sub reproducing the grouped-stream credit move (son55). adapt_via_conditioning is kept as supporting with sub null: the frozen executor adapts only through retrieved skills, but C03 requires an upstream phase that teaches the reader the conditioning schema, and the reader here is frozen. sol's generative_process_redesign is not kept: 'heuristic curation released as a free variable' restates the RL-curator premise, not a generative-procedure component.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A Qwen3-8B skill curator RL-trained on grouped ALFWorld streams produces a SkillRepo that raises held-out ALFWorld success (author-reported, 3 runs) over untrained, Gemini-prompted, and two heuristic memory baselines across four frozen executors.
assessment.not_supported: Consistent gains on reasoning/WebShop beyond noise; attribution of gains to skill content vs curator-weight priors; superiority over other RL-trained curators; efficiency in tokens; safety of update/delete ops.
unresolved: Opus: the test-time stream protocol (order, reset, passes, grouping) is unstated (opus:O01).

assessment.note: Author-reported results only; no reproduction by us. Improver level not claimed: training budget not matched against a prompt-optimised curator.

G.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. The bottleneck is specific: learning long-horizon curation (update/delete) of a persistent skill store from delayed, indirect feedback. Named neighbours: heuristic memory (ReasoningBank, MemP, run), skill-use RL (SkillRL, D2Skill) and short-stream RL curators (Wang 2025a, Ye 2026), with the residual 'short-horizon supervision'. Not 4: the RL-curator neighbours are neither run nor characterised beyond one sentence.

M.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. Grouped streams make later related tasks score earlier edits. Rollout-level GRPO over the whole curation sequence, plus a reward that excludes the first (empty-repo) task, is a reconstructable answer to delayed credit, and grouped vs random order is a checkable prediction. Weak points: the composite proxy terms (judge, compression), the uniform token advantage, and the self-judged outcome (opus:O02).

X.reason: Opus = sol. The operation chain is reconstructable: insert/update/delete function calls, ApplyOps after each task, BM25 top-5 read by the next task, prompts (App A) and hyperparameters (Table 4). Not 4: no admission gate beyond call validity, no rollback, version or size bound, and deletion is reported only as a share. Table 4's KL coefficient contradicts the text (opus:O05). The unstated test-stream protocol is scored once, in E.holdout (A2), as in the run's H-Mem precedent (static flow reconstructable, no gate → 3).

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. The metrics are environment-native and deterministic: ALFWorld goal-state SR (macro-averaged, steps counted over failed episodes), the WebShop programmatic reward, math_verify and GPQA exact match. Not 4: the self-judged curation signal is not validated, and there are two ≤0.2 text–table mismatches in secondary statements (opus:O03).
